actions.item: Check water supply piping for leaks; water overspent 165%
Spot-spray or poison wild oil palm seedlings, jungle woodies and creepers on trunks
Avoid overspraying palm circles; keep soft grasses for erosion control
Agree a contingency plan with purchasing and the agronomist for late fertiliser deliveries
Census palms in replanting areas before felling and shredding
Patrol roads in rain; add scupper drains and sumps
No over-pruning: keep 2 fronds below the last bunch in young mature fields; only dry fronds on Ganoderma palms
Reduce under-ripe bunches in young mature fields
Review machine productivity: 1 machine per 140 ha, 5 harvesters per machine, 12 t/machine-day
Adopt block harvesting (finish a field before moving)
Tackle about 10% of foreign workers earning below minimum wage through poor attendance
Remove old stumps and infected roots; plough and pulverise trunks in replanting
Continue deboling and mounding of Ganoderma palms under 20 years
Supply dead palms and fill vacant points in P23M and P25E
Continue rhinoceros beetle and Apogonia spraying in P24N
Harvest P22L carefully to avoid excessive frond removal
Raise workforce to 1 worker per 14 ha
Complete P25E planting (16,912 palms by Dec 2025)
Split PR25E (over 120 ha) into 2-3 sub-blocks
Keep closer to the fertiliser schedule (Mix B up to 2 months late; RP 63% by Mar 2026)
When fertiliser is late, apply to young and prime palms first
Place EFB 6-12 inches from the palm base in a ring; avoid excess
Tighten harvesting to about 15 days and improve supervision
Send collected loose fruit to the mill the same day
Remove dry hanging fronds
Keep the recommended frond stacking on high-silt soils
Cut crown-fracture palms 18 inches above the bend (P09B2)
Circle spray about 4 ft radius in low-stand grassy areas
Eradicate Clidemia and other seed-spread weeds in vacant-palm areas
Use one-sided or baffle nozzle covers on mist blowers; round nozzle in dense low-lying weeds
Bagworm: watch fresh damage, census, treat at 1st-4th instar when 10+ live larvae
Rat: post-baiting census, group sub-blocks into zones, bait in one direction
Install 5 more barn owl boxes along boundaries
P20H: avoid over-spraying and over-pruning

Build a drainage map on a digital elevation model and mark flood levels
Consider splash-cleaning mud from palm shoots after floods (Sg. Marung method)

Improve circle spraying in immature fields
Eradicate wild bitter gourd in P22L (Triclopyr 50 ml per pump)
Basal sanitation pruning in P22L
Blanket spray only once as a correction, then selective weeding
Monitor watermelon contractors' ploughing; no soil disturbance near palm rows

Complete the 2025 fertiliser programme

LADANG BUKIT JIN - FACT PACK (Far East Holdings Berhad, Far East group). Regional Senior Manager En. Musa Bin Abdul Halim. Estate Manager En. Muhammad Faiz Izzuddin Bin Mohd Bakri.

SOURCES. (1) PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisory), visit 12 March 2026, period reviewed January to December 2025, Planting Advisor En. Mohd Sufian Bin Yusoff. Previous PA 2/2025 visit 14 October 2025 (Jan-Sep 2025). (2) Agronomy Report 1/2026, visit 23 April 2026 (previous visit 17 November 2025), Senior Agronomist Mr. Lai Hong Heng; it revises the 2026 fertiliser programme. Earlier: Agronomy 2/2025 (17 Nov 2025, first 2026 programme) and Agronomy 1/2025 (6 Feb 2025, 2025 programme).

AREA (PA 1/2026, Dec 2025). Mature 1,648.60 ha (78.30%), immature 306.50 ha (14.56%), replanting 116.40 ha (5.53%), total planted 2,071.50 ha; buildings 5.50 ha; vacant 28.53 ha; title 2,105.53 ha. In 2026 the mature area falls to 1,602.70 ha: P22L 54.10 ha matured Jan 2026 and 100 ha of P00F goes to replanting. 647.80 ha (31.27%) is over 20 years old, mostly Ganoderma-infested. Topography flat to undulating with flood-prone low areas; monsoon Nov-Jan. Agro: Sep 2025 census average 130 palms/ha vs 148 at planting. 2026 age profile 0-3 yr 18%, 4-7 yr 9.95%, 8-19 yr 42.3%, 20-25 yr 29.9%. Replanting programme 2024 174.4 ha, 2025 116.4 ha, 2026 100 ha, 2027 100 ha, 2028 100 ha. Re-blocking Mar 2026: P00F 81.5 ha, P02C 279.5 ha, P22L 54.1 ha, P24N 213.3 ha, P25E 123.4 ha, P26F 100 ha.

CROP (PA 1/2026 section 8). Jan-Dec 2025 FFB 39,371.44 t vs budget 34,500.00 t (+14%), 23.88 t/ha vs budget 20.93; 2024 actual 40,710.19 t, 23.07 t/ha on 1,765 ha. CPO 7,372.53 t, OER 18.73%, KER 4.64%, CPO 4.47 t/ha. Highest fields P07D and P10A above 28 t/ha; lowest P00F. PA 2/2025: Jan-Sep 2025 28,966.57 t, 17.57 t/ha (budget 22,820 t; Jan-Sep 2024 32,725.71 t, 18.54 t/ha). Agro 1/2026 Table 19 Jan-Mar 2026 4.5 t/ha vs 3.69 Jan-Mar 2025 (+21.95%): P20H 3.32 (3.52), P00F 3.9 (2.57), P02C 4.4 (3.66), P03G 4.98 (3.79), P03J 3.96 (3.49), P07D 5.94 (4.81), P08K 4.54 (3.76), P09B 5.27 (3.79), P10A 4.66 (3.84), P22L new mature 0.98. Yield history (Agro chart) 2019 21.57, 2020 21.56, 2021 17.65, 2022 21.14, 2023 16.28, 2024 23.07, 2025 23.88 t/ha; PA Appendix 10 gives 2021 16.73, 2022 20.75, 2024 23.06. Block 2025 t/ha (PA App. 10): A 28.09, B 27.78, C 20.53, D 28.41, K 24.53, F 15.59, G 21.76, J 21.22, H 21.58. Harvesting rounds 104% of target 2024, 108% 2025, 107% to Mar 2026. No monthly tonnage printed in any report.

COST (PA 1/2026, Jan-Dec 2025, RM per t FFB). General charges 62.64 (budget 78.72), upkeep & cultivation 82.05 (106.26), harvesting & collection 74.89 (79.96); ex-estate 219.58 vs 264.94 (-17%). Processing 66.97, palm oil transport 7.45, cess 2.98, windfall tax 33.12 (budget 16.50), depreciation 9.32; grand total 339.42 vs 371.91. General charges RM3,098,842 = RM1,495.94/ha vs RM1,642.72 (-9%): management 490.82, labour & amenities 514.93, other 490.19 RM/ha. Overspends: executive salaries +7%, non-exec travel +25%, SOCSO +35%, training +7%, visiting agent +6%, EPF +69%, incentive +59%, recruitment +78% (52 TKIs vs 20 budgeted), renewal +17%, group insurance +50%, water +165% (check pipes), ISCC +118%. Upkeep RM/ha 2025: weeding 220.92 (243.30), manuring 1,321.23 (1,370.29), P&D 99.90 (202.67), census 3.97 (10.67), drains 26.17 (32.33), roads 149.06 (194.86), boundaries 16.15 (20.50), tools 2.25 (5.42), pruning 119.71 (143.67), total 1,959.38 (2,223.71). Harvesting RM52.17/t, internal transport RM22.71/t.

LABOUR (PA, Dec 2025). 151 workers (27 checkroll, 124 contract) vs requirement 135; 1 worker per 14 ha. Mature harvesters 93 vs 68 required; scout harvesters 14 vs 10; driver/loader 10/10; weeding 12/13; manuring 12/12; mandor 5/4; general 5/18. 64 recruited, 13 absconded, 28 went home in 12 months. About 10% of TKIs earned below minimum wage in H2 2025 because of poor attendance. Staff: Manager, 2 Assistant Managers, Executive Muhammad Nazhif (joined 15 Jul 2025), 5 supervisors, chief clerk, account clerk.

MECHANISATION (PA). 6 Timac (22 workers, 8.20 t/machine-day, 2.22 t/worker-day), 5 Long Star high-lift (24, 9.75, 2.03), 1 Iseki (5, 11.98, 2.71). Target 12 t per machine-day, 1 machine per 140 ha, 5 harvesters per machine. Harvesting interval 14 days in 2025, 25.92 rounds, over 90% ripe.

MANURING. 2025: all fertiliser applied (Agro: Mix B 475.7, GML 323.2, NK2 1,350, RP 194.15, Comp 44 51.6, Comp 25 20.65 t = 2,415.3 t; PA mature 2,192.55 t, immature 222.75 t). Mid-year Mix B delivery late; Timac semi-mechanised application from Aug 2025. 2026 to Mar: 642.7 of 737.55 t (87%); RP 159.4 of 254.25 t (63%), Mix B up to 2 months late. Agro 1/2026 AMENDED the 2026 programme: e.g. P10A/P09B Mix B 2,500 g Jan, RP 1,750-2,000 g Mar, Mix B 2,000 g Apr, 1,500 g Jul, 1,500 g Oct; P02C NK2 2,000 g Jan and Apr plus one Mix B 2,000 g round; P03G NK2 2,000 g x3; P03J NK2 8,000 g subsurface Jun; P07D/P08K Mix B 2,500/2,000/2,500/1,000 g plus RP 1,500-1,750 g; P20H Mix B 2,000 g Jan and Apr, RP 2,000 g, KIE 500 g, Mix B 1,500 g Jul and Oct; P22L Mix B 1,500 g x4 + RP 2,000 g; P23M Comp B 1,250-1,500 g x4 + RP 2,000 g; P24N Comp A 900-1,000 g x3 + RP 1,750 g; P25E Comp A 800 g Aug + RP 1,500 g Oct. New planting 600 g CRF + 500 g RP in planting hole. EFB: 2025 only P24N mulch 50.31 ha at 18 t/ha; Mar 2026 P25E 10.16 ha; keep EFB 6-12 inches off the palm base.

WEEDING. PA: selective spraying 94% and circle spraying 71% of the 2025 programme (printed figures do not compute). Agro Mar 2026 round 1 inter-row 95%, circle 67% (P09B 14%, P10A 52%). Soft grasses dominate; Nephrolepis beneficial in P03J1; undesirable weeds and incomplete kill in P08K1 and P10A3; Clidemia to be eradicated.

PESTS AND DISEASE. Ganoderma: PA 2025 census 431.60 ha, 66,292 points, 11,381 vacant, 20,124 infected = 47.52%. Agro 1/2025 trend (Ganoderma+vacant): P00F 24% (2020) to 62% (2024), P07D 3% to 34%, P02C 10% to 25%, P08K 5% to 25%. Mounding P00F, P00I (2018), P03G, P03J (2019), P02C2/C3 (2020), P02C1 (2021), P07D2 (2024); P02C and P03J 100% mounded. GanoFix trial P07D1 from Aug 2025 with new roots. Upper stem rot seen Nov 2025 in P09B2, P10A3, P10A6. Rat: 2025 Storm baiting 718.10 ha; damage resurged by Mar 2026, bait delayed, baiting from Apr 2026 (P10A 198.4, P09 55.7, P03G 69.20, P20H 152, P03J 89.20, P08K 71.5 ha done). 133 barn owl boxes, 100% occupancy; add 5 on boundaries. Bagworm treated on 684.21 ha in 2025 (Takumi, Dipel/Lipel; drones in P00F, P02C, P03G); Nov 2025 drone Takumi in P02C2, C3, C5, P08K2; Bravo in P07D; likely under control. 7,783 chains of predator host plants.

PRUNING. Progressive pruning 90% (1,476.50 of 1,648.60 ha) 2nd half 2025; P00F normal pruning twice a year due to frond snapping. Avoid over-pruning young mature (keep 2 fronds below last bunch) and Ganoderma palms (dry fronds only). Slight over-pruning P20H1/H2. Crown fracture palms in P09B2.

IMMATURE AND REPLANTING (PA section 11, Agro section 5). P22L (100 ha): 54.10 ha matured Jan 2026; 45.90 ha flooded area re-cambered and supplied (1,910 palms), merged with P24N; cost RM29,481.55/ha; wild bitter gourd, basal sanitation needed. P23M (32.10 ha): scout harvesting since Jun 2025, bund supply done Feb 2026, uneven growth in low areas, cost RM19,833.80/ha. P24N (174.40 ha): 14 months old Feb 2026, ablation started, 1,112 palms supplied, 148/ha, 120 ha ploughed by watermelon grower, cost RM10,628.42/ha. P25E (116.40 ha): 16,912 palms planted by Dec 2025 at 145/ha, cost RM6,748.43/ha. 2026 replanting P26F 100 ha (P00F1 74.20, P00F2 16.40, P02C3 9.40 ha): land prep from Apr 2026, felling & chipping 70%, planting from Nov 2026, full ploughing and pulverising because of high-silt subsoil. Watermelon integration encouraged; Mucuna where not taken up.

RAINFALL (PA App. 11). 2025 2,618 mm/125 days; 2024 2,417/126; 2023 1,986/124; 2022 2,348/127; 2021 2,337/109.

KEY ACTIONS. Fix water leaks; contingency plan for late fertiliser; machine productivity review; block harvesting; tighten harvesting to 15 days; post-baiting rat census and zone baiting; 5 more owl boxes; split PR25E; census immature blocks after each supply; DEM flood map and higher bunds; splash-cleaning after floods; Clidemia and wild bitter gourd control; basal sanitation in P22L.
